Sarawak MM2H application guide (amended 31 July 2025, 35 pages): eligibility (age 30+, countries with diplomatic relations except Israel and North Korea), financial proof (RM500,000 fixed deposit plus RM10,000/15,000 monthly pension or offshore income, or RM100,000/200,000 savings), required documents, security/personal bond rates by nationality, conditions (RM250,000 minimum FD balance, 30 days a year), work rules (part-time up to 20 hours a week; minority JV share up to 49% of RM250,000 paid-up capital), RM5,000 processing fee, 50% FD withdrawal after one year, optional house purchase minimums, 5+5-year pass and renewal, panel banks and clinics; plus a general note on Sarawak (area, population) out of scope. This pass added 18 rules: processing fee, security bond rates by nationality (8), RM15,000 income with dependant, savings alternatives (2), 50% FD withdrawal, optional house purchase minimums (2), child age limit, passport validity, good-conduct letter age, renewal filing deadline. Not recorded as out of scope: part-time work-hour limit and the joint-venture paid-up capital (business conditions, not the residence route), medical insurance for under-60s (no amount).

Presidential Decree UP-5611 of 5 January 2019 on tourism development, current edition (to 5 June 2023): tourism concept 2019-2025 and road maps (Annexes 1-4), visa categories and consular fees (Annex 5, para 4: out of scope), para 5 residence permit for buyers of real estate (USD 300,000 Tashkent city and region after UP-101 of 8 April 2022; USD 200,000 six regions; USD 100,000 Karakalpakstan and other regions), Annex 6 list of 111 eligible countries (wording of UP-52 of 15 January 2022), working group (Annexes 7-8). Tourism export figures in the concept are out of scope. This pass added the Annex 6 list as a rule (eligible_countries: 111, with ISO codes) and the 15 January 2022 replacement of the list as an event.

Executive Order 63 of 7 November 1986 (in force immediately): Special Investor Resident Visa for aliens investing at least US$50,000 in tourist-related projects or establishments (investor, spouse, unmarried minor children), conditions (two visits a year of at least seven days each, annual report), exemptions from immigration fees, remittance and repatriation rights, inter-agency committee. This pass added 3 rules: 7 days per visit, two visits a year, annual report.

Omnibus Investments Code (Executive Order 226, 16 July 1987, in force on approval): Board of Investments, investment priorities and incentives for registered enterprises (out of scope), foreign investments without incentives, regional headquarters and warehouses (out of scope), Book V Special Investors Resident Visa (US$75,000 minimum, US$50,000 for those under EO 63 and EO 1037, annual report; visa expires if the investment is withdrawn), repeals. This pass added 2 rules: the US$50,000 amount for EO 63/1037 investors and the annual report.

Decree-Law 50/83/M of 17 December 1983 (to take effect 1 January 1984; revoked by DL 3/84/M): residence in Macau for holders of capital investments recognised by the Governor as of particular interest (property, businesses, company holdings, promises), family of up to six, application procedure, one-year renewable permits, fees (1,000 patacas per permit or renewal; 500 patacas per certificate of start of residence for persons under the 1969 regulation). No investment amounts (left to the Governor's order). This pass added 4 rules: up to six family members, one-year validity, 1,000-pataca permit fee, 500-pataca certificate fee (noted as possibly not the investor route). Not recorded: procedural deadlines (at least 30 days to complete a file) and age 14 thresholds for documents.

Decree-Law 3/84/M of 28 January 1984 (effective from 1 January 1984), replacing DL 50/83/M with the same scheme: residence for holders of investments in projects the Governor recognises as of particular interest, family of up to six, one-year renewable permits, fees (1,000 patacas per permit or renewal; 500 patacas per certificate of start of residence). No investment amounts (left to the Governor's order). This pass added 4 rules: up to six family members, one-year validity, 1,000-pataca permit fee, 500-pataca certificate fee (noted as possibly not the investor route). Not recorded: procedural deadlines and age 14 thresholds for documents.

Regulations on Hong Kong and Macao residents entering Taiwan and residence/settlement, version amended 6 August 2001 (39 articles): entry and stay permits, residence grounds incl. investment of NT$5 million (art. 16(1)(5)) and NT$5 million remitted and deposited for one year (art. 16(1)(6)), guarantors, residence certificate validity (1 year 6 months to 3 years) and one-year extensions, revocation (incl. under 183 days a year), settlement after one year continuous or two years with 270 days a year (30 days' absence allowed). This pass added 9 rules: deposit holding period, certificate validity range (2), extension length, 183-day presence, settlement periods (2), 270-day presence, 30-day absence. Not recorded (out of scope, general entry rules): visitor permit and stay periods, guarantor limit of five a year, refusal periods.

Same regulations, version amended 10 June 2014 (40 articles): residence grounds incl. investment of NT$6 million (art. 17(1)(5)); deposit ground dropped with a three-year transition (art. 30); certificate validity 1 year 6 months to 3 years; extensions up to two years; settlement after one year continuous or two years continuous with 270 days a year, 30 days' absence allowed. This pass added 9 rules (certificate validity range, extension length, settlement periods, 270-day presence, 30-day absence, transitional deposit amount and window) and 1 event (deposit ground dropped). Not recorded (out of scope): general entry and stay rules, refusal periods, other residence grounds.

Amendment history of the Hong Kong and Macao residence regulations: 20 entries from first issue (30 June 1997, 38 articles) to the amendment of 13 June 2022, listing the articles changed each time and transfers of competence; no rule texts or numbers. This pass added 7 events: the first issue (as legal basis, investment ground not shown), the full revisions of 2009 and 2018, and the amendments touching the residence-grounds article in 2002, 2004, 2021 and 2022. The 1999 full revision and the 2014 amendment are already events from the version texts; amendments that touched only other articles (entry permits, guarantors, documents) are not recorded.

Immigration Act (入出國及移民法), full revision promulgated 26 December 2007 (97 articles; in force 1 August 2008): entry and exit, residence and settlement of nationals without household registration (incl. investment ground, art. 9(1)(6)), foreigners' residence (incl. investor ground, art. 23(1)(4)), permanent residence (incl. investment immigration, art. 25(4), and revocation under 183 days a year, art. 33), deportation, migration agencies (investment-immigration fund brokerage rules, art. 56, fines art. 79), penalties. This pass added 14 rules and proposes 2 programmes (foreign investor residence; investment route for nationals without household registration), whose amounts the Act leaves to regulations. Not recorded: ordinary (non-investment) permanent residence periods (5 years with 183 days, art. 25(1)), general entry and refusal rules, and penalties not tied to investment immigration.

Amendment history of Taiwan's Immigration Act: 12 entries from enactment (21 May 1999, 70 articles) to the amendment of 28 June 2023, with the articles changed and the in-force dates set by the Executive Yuan; no rule texts or numbers. Already recorded: the 2007 full revision in force 1 August 2008 (launch of investment-immigration permanent residence).
